column7: 2026-11-06: Retry-After work is on hold: the user wants to look at their 429 dashboards first, so don't start it until they say so. Decided by the user: wait the Retry-After time PLUS the normal backoff delay (not instead of it, not the max of the two). Reason: billing's Retry-After is the moment their rate window reopens, and ~40 pods returning at that exact moment get 429'd again; the backoff on top spreads them out. Client already sets error.retryAfter in seconds. Not yet decided: the API shape (my suggestion was an option that returns a delay in ms, called where calculateDelay is, so retryDelay in the callbacks includes it), whether maxTimeout caps the Retry-After part, what happens when it doesn't fit in maxRetryTime (today the wait is shortened with Math.min), and whether randomize applies to it. Ask the user about those before building.

2026-11-06: The user lifted the hold on Retry-After work (said 'build it now'), but then stopped for the day before answering the open design questions, so nothing is built yet. Next session: ask them to confirm (or say 'go with your recommendations') on these four points. They are MY recommendations, not user decisions: (1) API: a retryAfter(error) => ms option called where calculateDelay is (index.js ~183) so retryDelay includes it; alternative is auto-reading numeric error.retryAfter by default, which the user's wording hinted at; (2) maxTimeout caps only the backoff part, not Retry-After, because Retry-After is the server's reopen time; (3) if Retry-After plus backoff doesn't fit maxRetryTime, stop and throw rather than shorten with Math.min, because retrying before the window reopens wastes an attempt; (4) randomize applies to the backoff part only. Still the user's decision: wait = Retry-After PLUS backoff. Working tree already has uncommitted changes in index.js, index.d.ts, index.test-d.ts, readme.md, test.js: build on top of them, don't revert.
